focus: a complete KTZ-style dependency chain ending in one global polynomial and exponent $1-o(1)$

messages.body_markdown: The round-2 audit leaves `E2E-15` as the principal incidence obligation. Please prove the exact algebra-aware alternative with $D\le K_\theta d$ and $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ retained mass. The fractional-cover and collision calculations of researcher-0008 show that a graph-only cover-or-energy statement is insufficient.
messages.subject: Exact low-weight dichotomy still needed

messages.body_markdown: The factor lift in `E2E-22` is mathematically valid with one simple seed: formal implicit uniqueness gives $Q$, and more than $\Delta$ graph lines force $C(X,Y,Q)=0$. Please resubmit it as a standalone exact lemma. Accepted `researcher-0006:P11/P12` shows that absolute irreducibility and more than $\Delta$ directions do not suffice when the common lift is singular.
messages.subject: Submit the simple-seed factor lift

messages.body_markdown: The bound $D=O_\theta(d)$ is doing two independent jobs: it makes the accepted whole-relation cleanup cost $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable below $\epsilon$, and it bounds the factor list by $O_\theta(1)$. If $D$ acquires an inverse power of $\epsilon$, `E2E-20` and `E2E-21` both fail and the longer factorwise/cross-factor route is again necessary.
messages.subject: Why bounded weight closes both losses

nodes.label: Bivariate line-versus-point instance
nodes.notes: The scope is exactly $m=2$, prime field, and $100<d<p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: Fix a prime $p$, an integer $100<d<p$, a function $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and a polynomial $P_L\in\mathbb F_p[t]$ with $\deg P_L\le d$ for every affine line $L$. Define $$\rho=\frac d p,\qquad \epsilon=\Pr_{L,\,x\in L}[P_L(x)=f(x)],\qquad \operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$

nodes.label: Accepted graph and completion predicate
nodes.notes: The normalization makes edge mass directly comparable with point agreement.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(x,L):x\in L,\ P_L(x)=f(x)\}.$$ For an accepted subgraph $G=(X,T,E)$ put $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)}.$$ For $c>0$, let $\mathsf{Done}_c$ mean that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c\epsilon$.

nodes.label: Fixed-exponent reduction
nodes.notes: It suffices to build the engine for $0<\theta\le1/4$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For fixed $\eta>0$, set $\theta=\min\{\eta,1/4\}$. Then $$0<\theta\le\frac14,
\qquad \rho^{1-\eta}\ge\rho^{1-\theta}.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component measures
nodes.notes: This starts the exact accepted component-level KTZ chain.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be a connected accepted graph of minimum degree $k$, and put $\tau=|T|/[p(p+1)]$. If $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\frac{|X|}{p^2}\ge\frac{k}{4p},
\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ reaching family
nodes.notes: This selector is cardinality-based and component-local.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Under `E2E-04`, there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4|T|}{k}\le|R|\le\frac{16|T|}{k},
\qquad |R|\ge p+1,$$ and every $L\in T$ has more than half of its accepted neighbors incident to a line of $R\setminus\{L\}$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ weighted interpolant
nodes.notes: Its degree depends on the cardinality of the reaching family.
nodes.statement_markdown: Put $$D=16\left(\left\lfloor\sqrt{d|R|}\right\rfloor+1\right).$$ There is a nonzero squarefree $A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ with $\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D$, $A_Z\not\equiv0$, and $$A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\qquad(M\in R).$$ Moreover, $D/k<1/5000$ and $D<k\le p<|R|$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ root extension
nodes.notes: More than $D$ reached roots force every restriction identity.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ characteristic-safe cleanup
nodes.notes: The resultant argument is valid in the full campaign regime.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree and has total degree below $p$. There is a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$ and an exceptional edge set satisfying $$|E_{\rm exc}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Outside $E_{\rm exc}$, the $B$-identity holds and $\mathcal DB$ is nonzero at every retained accepted incidence.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ clean core
nodes.notes: Connectivity may fragment during peeling.
nodes.statement_markdown: One has $$\frac{|E_{\rm exc}|}{|E|}<\frac1{4000}.$$ Peeling vertices below $k_1=\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty accepted graph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $k_1$.

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ simple roots
nodes.notes: Two retained directions convert generic derivative nonvanishing into vertical simplicity.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Every point vertex $x$ of $G_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Accepted KTZ component decoder
nodes.notes: The conclusion is one polynomial, not a list.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `E2E-04`, there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root frontier
nodes.notes: The small-component antecedent is not implied by local agreement.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $k_0=\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If a component of the KTZ-pruned core has line measure $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac d p\right)^{1/2},$$ then one degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/160000$.

nodes.label: Universal reaching-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: The decoder branch in `E2E-15` is indispensable. Researcher-0008 provisionally strengthens this to fractional reaching and sharp quadratic collision energy.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$, there is a legal constant-label table with $$\frac1{2K}\le\epsilon\le\frac2K$$ such that every family reaching half of every accepted line has $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ although a constant polynomial already has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Rank-reaching relation interface
nodes.notes: Restriction rank replaces the size of a universal selected-line family.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For $d\le D<p$, put $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\}$$ and $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},
\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For an accepted $G=(X,T,E)$, define $$\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E,
\ \exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ (x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching when $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<\dim V_D$, and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Bounded-weight rank-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the main open incidence bottleneck. The relation degree must be $O_\theta(d)$, not $d$ times an inverse power of $\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every fixed $0<\theta\le1/4$, there exist $C_\theta,K_\theta>0$ and $0<a_\theta,c_\theta\le1$ such that, whenever $$\epsilon\ge C_\theta\rho^{1-\theta},$$ either $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta}$ holds, or there are an accepted graph $G=(X,T,E)$, a set $R\subseteq T$, and an integer $D$ such that $$e(G)\ge a_\theta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\theta d,$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Near-linear parameter gate
nodes.notes: Increasing the threshold constant is harmless; if the trigger exceeds one, the implication is vacuous.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the relation branch, $$\frac{D}{\epsilon p}\le\frac{K_\theta}{C_\theta}\rho^\theta.$$ After enlarging $C_\theta$ so that $C_\theta\ge10^5K_\theta/a_\theta$, one has $$D\le\frac{a_\theta\epsilon p}{10^5}<p.$$

nodes.label: Squarefree rank-kernel relation
nodes.notes: Take a kernel element and then its squarefree radical. The domain property preserves every selected-line identity; $|R|>D$ excludes a base-only relation.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For the rank-reaching tuple in the relation branch, there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0\quad(M\in R).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching root extension
nodes.notes: This is the accepted root-count argument with rank-reaching as the input interface; the strengthened statement still needs a standalone audit.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every line vertex $L\in T$, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0.$$

nodes.label: Whole-relation cleanup at bounded weight
nodes.notes: The exact accepted cleanup is sufficient here because `E2E-16` makes its $O(D/p)$ loss a small fraction of $\epsilon$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content in $Z$. Then $B$ is primitive in $Z$, squarefree, $Z$-dependent, and of total degree below $p$. There are a formal directional derivative $\mathcal D$ and an exceptional set $E_{\rm exc}\subseteq E$ such that $$\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1,
\qquad |E_{\rm exc}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$ Every line incident to $E\setminus E_{\rm exc}$ satisfies the $B$-identity, and $\mathcal DB$ is nonzero at every edge of $E\setminus E_{\rm exc}$.

nodes.label: Global clean simple-root core
nodes.notes: Exceptional deletion costs at most $(D/p)^2+D/p$; peeling at degree $D$ costs less than $2D/p$. Two retained directions force vertical simplicity.
nodes.statement_markdown:
After enlarging $C_\theta$ by a constant depending only on $a_\theta,K_\theta$, deleting $E_{\rm exc}$ and iteratively deleting vertices of current degree at most $D$ leaves an accepted graph $G_1=(X_1,T_1,E_1)$ satisfying $$e(G_1)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2}\epsilon,
\qquad \operatorname{mindeg}(G_1)>D.$$ Every $L\in T_1$ satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every $x\in X_1$ satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Bounded factor partition and heavy class
nodes.notes: Vertical simplicity makes factor assignment unique at both ends of every edge, so each factor class preserves degrees. The cited source is exact-audited but revise-grade.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i$$ into distinct irreducibles and put $\Delta_i=\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}C_i$. Then every $C_i$ depends on $Z$ and $$s\le\deg_ZB\le\frac D d\le K_\theta.$$ The graph $G_1$ partitions into factor classes $F_i$, each preserving all vertex degrees and satisfying $$C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0,
\qquad C_i(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0.$$ For some $i$, $$e(F_i)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon,
\qquad \operatorname{mindeg}(F_i)>D\ge\Delta_i.$$

nodes.label: High-direction factor linearization
nodes.notes: Researcher-0003:P7 states this exact factor-sensitive lift, but its enclosing source is audit-inexact. Researcher-0001:P7 and researcher-0007:P6 certify nearby component-level templates. A fresh exact standalone audit remains necessary.
nodes.statement_markdown: For the heavy class $F_i$, there exist $u\in\mathbb F_p^\times$ and $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ such that $$C_i=u(Z-Q).$$ Consequently, $$Q(x)=f(x)$$ for every point vertex $x$ of $F_i$.

nodes.label: Vinh-free aggregation to one polynomial
nodes.notes: Once the irreducible factor is $Z-Q$, all of its disconnected classes charge to the same algebraic polynomial.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the relation branch, if $X_i$ and $E_i$ are the point and edge sets of the heavy class, then $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{|X_i|}{p^2}\ge\frac{|E_i|}{p^2(p+1)}=e(F_i)\ge\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\epsilon.$$ Together with the direct branch of `E2E-15`, this proves $\mathsf{Done}_{c_\theta^*}$ for $$c_\theta^*=\min\left\{c_\theta,\frac{a_\theta}{2K_\theta}\right\}.$$

nodes.label: Close every fixed exponent
nodes.notes: All constants depend only on the fixed exponent parameter.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$, there are $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\rho^{1-\eta}$$ implies that some $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ with $\deg_{\rm tot}Q\le d$ satisfies $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Uniform exact-linear endpoint
nodes.notes: This stronger statement is refuted at the legal degree $d=101$. It does not refute any fixed-$\eta$ target.
nodes.statement_markdown: There exist absolute constants $C,c>0$ such that every legal instance satisfying $$\epsilon\ge C\frac d p$$ also satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Accepted singular-lift obstruction
nodes.notes: This accepted round-2 obstruction makes the simple-root conclusion in `E2E-20` logically indispensable for the proposed lift.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p>4d+1$ and $D=2d$, there is an absolutely irreducible $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ of weighted degree $D$ supporting more than $D$ distinct degree-at-most-$d$ formal graph lines through one base point, while no $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ satisfies $C(X,Y,Q(X,Y))\equiv0$. On every supported graph, all $D-d$ vertically ramified lifts are singular.

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate soundness
nodes.notes: The goal remains blocked on `E2E-15` and a fresh exact audit of the rank-kernel, cleanup-transfer, and factor-linearization chain. Work states do not assert proof status.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, and every legal bivariate line table, $$\operatorname{Agr}_{\rm LVP}(f,P)\ge C_\eta\left(\frac d p\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies that there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\operatorname{Agr}_{\rm LVP}(f,P).$$

summary: Round 2 preserves the exact accepted KTZ component chain `E2E-04`–`E2E-12`, whose available unconditional machinery stops at the square-root frontier. The near-linear spine is `E2E-15`–`E2E-24`: an algebra-aware rank-or-decode dichotomy must retain $\Omega_\theta(\epsilon)$ mass while producing weighted degree $D=O_\theta(d)$. That bound makes the accepted whole-relation cleanup loss $O_\theta(d/p)$ absorbable and leaves only $O_\theta(1)$ irreducible factors. A heavy simple factor then linearizes as $Z-Q$, and all of its edges—across disconnected components—charge to one global polynomial without Vinh mixing. The factor lift is mathematically supported but lacks a fresh exact-accepted standalone source. Accepted round-2 singular-pencil examples show that its simple-root hypothesis cannot be weakened to absolute irreducibility, smooth resultants, or high direction count alone. The goal remains blocked on the low-weight incidence dichotomy and exact audits of the strengthened algebraic transfers; the uniform $Cd/p$ endpoint remains separately refuted.
target_statement: Prove that soundness at least $(d/p)^{1-o(1)}$ yields agreement with one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial for $100<d<p$ over $\mathbb F_p$.
title: End-to-end soundness chain
